title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector assistance to IDPs and Host communities in Tselemti Woreda and Maytsebry town of North Gonder Zone, Amhara Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project targets Mai-tsebri town and Tselemt woredas of North Gonder Zone, Amhara Region. The objective of the project is to provide dignified, Rights-based integrated multi sectoral humanitarian assistance to displacement and conflict affected populations to meet immediate lifesaving needs, provide safe and inclusive access to essential services, and contribute to a well-coordinated response that ensures gender, protection, accountability to affected people (AAP), and (PSEA) are well integrated. The response shall benefit from complimentary and sequenced consortium organizations funding streams from BHA, SIDA, NMFA and ECHO. The Project shall focus on Health, Nutrition, Protection, Agriculture and WASH support. The agriculture part is founded on a cash and markets-based approach which recognizes the increased improvement in markets and shall use and support local markets.ltbrgtAll targeted 43,548 beneficiaries will receive multi-core competency support simultaneously with a total budget of 1.2 M USD. Disability and potential protection risk exposure will be key areas of attention. ltbrgtThe Protection component and mainstreaming will focus on assisting IDPs for entitlement to HLPs and legal assistance, reducing the vulnerability of IDPs to risk and human rights violations. The agriculture component shall focus on input supply and capacity building to support restoration of crop and livestock production and multipurpose cash to enable drought and conflict affected people meet their basic needs. ltbrgtThe health part does include primary health care services including consultations for communicable and non-communicable diseases, management for injuries, ERW case treatment and referral service, child health care services including routine immunization, nutrition screening and linkage, integrated MHPSS services and integrated MISP for SRH services including family planning counseling and service provision, ANC, PNC, syndromic treatment of STIs and CMR/IPV. Additionally, health education on priority diseases and conditions and health and hygiene promotion will also be provided under integrated PHC services. The proposed health interventions will also improve access to basic PHC and referral services for vulnerable drought-affected communities and ERW cases by providing first aid kits and supporting the referral by providing fuel to ambulances. Through the health sector it is planned to reach 17,358 drought affected communities(gtwomen-5,989,gtmen-6,075,The Nutrition section plans to provide lifesaving nutrition interventions by integration of CMAM and IYCF-E activities through the existing health system. Major activities planned under the project are to improve the capacity of 33 health facilities (27 OTPs and 6 SCs.) support regular U5 and PLW screening and find and treat campaigns, Family MUAC, supply transportation, procurement and provision of routine drugs, OTP/SC materials and recording formats., training in CMAM and IYCF-E and CMAM for health service providers. In the project period IMC plans to Screen (18,313children under five and 6,522 PLWs). ltbrgtThe WASH results are Categorized in four components each with detail activities relevant to contribute for each output Improve access to Water supply and sanitation facility (equitable and affordable access to enough safe water to meet their drinking and domestic needs improved access to Hygiene promotion that supports behaviors, community engagement, and actions to reduce the risk of disease is fundamental to a successful WASH response: improved access and Use of hygiene items or Standard WASH-NFI , and improved solid waste management. Generally, the WASH programs response will contribute to reduce nutrition and public health risks and scope of activities are promoting good hygiene practices through active community engagement and encourage people to take their own action, providing safe and adequate water supply. The project duration is one year, from May 15, 2024, to May 14, 2025. ltbrgtlt/pgt
